# Stage contracts and CI/CD pathways

Where the Librarian already declares a stage's tools and exit gate, where it does not, and the checks that would let a tool attach to the stage of the workflow it serves. The model to copy exists: for each MCP session purpose, standard/phases.yaml declares its phases, each phase's tool bundle and its exit gate (named checks in a closed registry, validated when the Core starts; phases.py). Since M1b (26 November) the batch's stages are declared the same way, in standard/stages.yaml. Provenance: C = read from the code; P = proposed here. Proposed and unaccepted; CI can check the declarations, not the runtime behaviour of the to-be flows.

## Where stages are declared today

| Surface | Declared today | Tools bound to | Exit gate | Gap | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MCP sessions | 8 purposes and their phases, as data | each phase's bundle | named checks, the registry validated at start | none: the model to copy | C: phases.py 1-10 and 180, standard/phases.yaml |
| The batch (UC1b, UC1c) | since M1b, as data: 9 source and 3 folder stages, each with its tools, the stages it depends on, its recipe, model use, risk and role | each stage's own tools; a call outside them is reported in the run log, and refused once enforce is refuse | named checks (result_status), recorded on the stage's result; recipes read from the declaration (MF-020) | enforcement is report-only until a clean run; a stage changed without its recipe bump is not yet caught in CI | C: standard/stages.yaml, stages.py, batch.py |
| Workflows and pipelines | 19 workflows and 2 pipelines, as YAML; since M1b each compiles to a manifest (process_manifest) | each step's action | macro preconditions and checkpoints; a parent's mandate is checked from the manifest | a step does not name the process stage it serves, so its tools cannot be checked against that stage | C: standard/workflows/intake-to-stage.yaml, manifests.py |
| Folder review to Geo-Grapher | not declared | the Geo-Grapher service the Core starts per library | the receipt contract, in a report table only | geo_service.py reads no receipt fields, so changed_entity_ids is not enforced | C: geo_service.py; the receipt-contract table |
| These to-be flows | drawn, unaccepted | lanes and labels | the Oracle's Tier A at each level | specifications belong in the Core (policy); these are not yet a runtime declaration | policy lines 84-87 |

## A stage contract (proposed)

| Field | What it says | Checked by | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| stage | the process and the stage, e.g. ingestion / enrichment / parse | the Core | at load, as phases.yaml is |
| tools | the tools that may run at this stage; any other is refused, naming its rule | the Broker, per call | at run time |
| entry | the receipt the previous stage must have emitted | the Core | at run time |
| exit gate | named deterministic checks from the closed registry | the Oracle's Tier A | at run time |
| receipt | what the stage emits, hashed, so an unchanged child is reused by its hash | the Oracle (`oracle:tiera`) | at run time |
| recipe | the version of what the stage does: a changed recipe invalidates reuse, as a CI cache key does | CI: a stage's code changed without a recipe bump fails | in CI |
| risk | the stage's level from the authority table, so a high-risk stage in a run no tier 0 oversees holds for the Owner | the Core | at run time |
| role | the lane that runs it | the Core | at load |

## Where tools attach, by stage

| Stage | Tools that belong there | Gate before it moves on | Where in the to-be |

| folder screen | the folder survey (folder_review.py), the Clerk's screen | the screened set; a sensitivity flag goes out | `folder-review:folderscreen` |
| group apply | Geo-Grapher graph-building | the receipt matches the decision | `folder-review:geoapply`, `folder-review:dgeo` |
| capture | ingest, intake_run, queue_source, read_url | an immutable capture with its hash | `source-intake:capture` |
| parse | pdf_to_markdown, ocr_pdf, the structure survey | the page map and the conversion check | `source-parse:parse` |
| read | deep_read, clerk_next and clerk_submit | bounded tasks within the cap | `source-reading:read` |
| relate | dik_rebuild | coverage before relations | `source-reading:relate` |
| claim review | the claim review | closed verdicts only | `verify-claims:review` |
| accept | staging_decide | the attestation names who accepted | `acceptance:leadaccept` |
| publish | Geo-Grapher paper-import | a receipt with the stored link | `paper-publication:publish` |
| findability | index, views_refresh | findable in Search and the catalogue | `ingestion:doracle` |
| research rounds | search, research_round, web_search, the graph_find and graph_read groups | candidates from the corpus only | `research:rounds` |
| delegation | delegate, dispatch_plan, Geo-Grapher's compile_task_packet | every citation verified | `delegate:cite` |

## Repository CI and CD pathways (proposed)

| Pathway | What it checks | What it catches | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Pack check | render_pack.py --check --all on any push that touches these packs | a view older than its spec, a broken cross-system reference, an unquoted comma | C: no test runs the renderer; the 26 November UC-G5 defect passed CI |
| 2. A reports-only path | a push that changes only reports/ or docs/ runs the pack check and the plan test, not the full Windows matrix | the full matrix spent on prose (it ran for each of the last three reports-only commits) | C: ci.yml runs on every push with no paths filter; tests/test_ci_workflows.py holds the workflow to its rules, so the change must keep them |
| 3. Stage-contract check | every stage declares its tools, gate, receipt and recipe; every gate check is registered; a stage changed without its recipe bump fails | a tool attached to the wrong stage; stale output reused | C: phases.py validate_checks does this for sessions only |
| 4. Tool-to-stage coverage | each MCP tool belongs to a phase bundle or a stage, or is marked as usable at any stage | a new tool with no stage, open everywhere | C: the tool decorator records tier and effect, not a stage (tools/delegate.py 37) |
| 5. Geo-Grapher receipt contract | a JSON schema for the receipt (the receipt-contract table's fields), checked against a fixture in both repositories' CI | changed_entity_ids or the stored link silently dropped | C: geo_service.py reads no receipt fields; Geo-Grapher's contracts/ has wire and trace schemas, no receipt schema |
| 6. Geo-Grapher hosted CI | Geo-Grapher's own suite on each push | a wheel the Librarian pins, built untested | C: the Geo-Grapher repository has no .github folder; it has a release manifest and baseline digests (contracts/v1.1) |
| 7. The wheel pin (CD) | a Geo-Grapher release that passes its CI and the receipt contract moves the Librarian's pin through a reviewed change | GEOGRAPHER_TOO_OLD found when a library starts instead of in CI | C: geo_service.py 4 and 140 |
| 8. Workflow declarations | every standard workflow and pipeline loads, its actions exist, and each step names its stage | a workflow that fails at its first run, or a step at the wrong stage | C: tests/test_workflow_steps.py tests the step engine; whether it loads every standard workflow was not checked here |

## The order that pays first

- 1 and 2 cost little and protect these packs at once.
- 5 and 6 close the gap the weave exposed: the Librarian now handles each Geo-Grapher outcome on paper, but nothing checks that the receipt carries the fields those outcomes depend on.
- 3 and 4 are the runtime pathway: once the batch's stages are declared like the session phases, a tool attaches to its stage, and the Broker refuses it anywhere else.
